treatment: No narrower exception is recorded. Adopt the live reader-facing clause in independent wording under the local authority order.
Google's conjunction advice yields to the house rule for the intended logical relationship.
The requirement-language section owns modal meanings. Retain could for a genuine condition or past situation.
Adopt Google's advice on example placement. Introduce the example with commas, parentheses, a colon, or a separate sentence.
Adopt Google's avoidance intent. Use the British form grey only when the underlying term remains necessary; governed source forms retain their spelling.
Introduce an open list with for example, such as, or a category name. Omit etc. and and so on.
The inclusive-language rules own generic pronouns, named roles, and a person's stated pronouns.
Use the selected British dictionary for the ordinary word. For a governed product or project designation, apply the official-name rules instead of importing Google's one-word form.
Preserve 2-Step Verification as Google's official feature name. Lowercase generic verification wording.
Apply the Android entry only in Android documentation. Another platform's official interaction model and labels control its instructions.
These entries concern deprecated or product-specific Google names. Use the current official name unless the passage identifies a historical interface.
Keep the entry's meanings, casing, shortening, command names, and console vocabulary within Google Cloud or its named product.
Use the control rules when naming a UI element and the interaction rules when describing its action. These entries govern documentation about the interface, not the interface copy itself.
Apply a platform, product, version, CLI, or GUI condition only when it matches the documented host. ISO records and governed host forms take precedence.
Prefer a direct description or define downscope on first use. Preserve it when the applicable security or IAM authority defines the operation.
Use Google as a product name, not a generic verb. Preserve official lifecycle labels and lowercase generic lifecycle terms.
The literal-formatting rules govern exact symbols in code, data, names, and literals. Use ordinary words or a precise prose verb elsewhere.
Use descriptive placeholders and actions in reader-facing prose. Preserve exact code, filenames, commands, and visible labels.
The authority that defines the protocol, API, security, lifecycle, or infrastructure concept controls its normative meaning.
Establish the concept under its governing authority before applying Google's reader-facing casing or formatting.
A governed technical or product designation controls its form; a general spelling preference does not replace it.
Distinguish ordinary prose from product, CLI, markup, UI, document-type, and command designations. Exact host or source terminology controls.
Preserve a current or historical Google product or API term only in its named scope. Product documentation defines the object.
Apply control naming to labels and accessible names. For an action or feature state, apply the interaction rules. Preserve a defined analytics term within its source scope.
Use the applicable measurement, technology, product, or host authority. Distinguish bits from bytes. Use Google's form only in governed scope or exact source text.
Prefer a direct description in ordinary prose. Retain a formally defined testing, monitoring, or security method under its governing authority.
Use allow, deny, or block terminology in original prose. Identify an unavoidable exact non-inclusive term only where readers must match it; use the selected prose term elsewhere.
Use factual community terminology for people and a direct description for a loose system metaphor. For a formally defined technical use of blind, apply its field authority under the definition rules.
Replace the generic slur or metaphor with its intended meaning. Preserve GIMP as the official application name and identify any unavoidable exact literal.
Preserve a defined IAM, product, source, or interface concept. Otherwise name the precise action or identifier type.
Use the applicable legal, privacy, security, contractual, or project authority for a classification. An editorial example does not establish that classification.
Replace an unqualified easy task claim with the actual requirement or measured usability. Retain stated complexity and official names.

Apply the current entry's guidance on first use, grammar, capitalisation, compounds, and precision under the English word-choice rules. For an abbreviation, apply the abbreviation rules. Preserve an established source or technical meaning; otherwise use a direct ordinary-language alternative.
Use the applicable product, protocol, security, networking, filesystem, or health-data authority for meaning. Google's clause governs only reader-facing form.

Review the technical or figurative expression for inclusive wording. Describe the measurable condition, action, role, or physical characteristic. Preserve an exact governed designation within its scope.
Use precise countries, mobile terms, dates, events, and literal training language under the internationalisation rules, unless a governed term is required.
Apply the entry's context-sensitive prefix or compound rule with source and product exceptions. A house-style example does not establish a universal form.
Apply the entry's plural and grammatical-number distinction. Preserve the established convention of the applicable field.
Apply the entry's complete conjunction pattern and semantic distinction; retain every element needed to state that relationship.
Use that is in technical prose. When APA writing style is selected, apply its Latin-abbreviation treatment within that scope.
For this Google adaptation, expand contractions in original technical prose. Use let us only when that meaning is necessary.
The requirement-language section owns the permission, capability, and possibility meanings that replace Google's modal preference.
State a requirement, procedure, or failure message directly. Retain please only for a genuine request for permission or forgiveness, or in preserved correspondence.
Preserve persist as an established API, state, or code term. Otherwise describe the persistent state or use make persistent.
Use PostgreSQL as the official product name in original prose. Preserve an exact Postgres interface label where the host uses it.
Use a hyphen or slash when the relationship needs a connector. In selected ASD prose, apply the adopted punctuation rules.
Apply a named Google Cloud or product meaning only in that scope. A product example elsewhere does not restrict the general entry to that product.
Apply the general editorial clause even when Google illustrates it with a Cloud example. Use the documented platform's designation.
Apply an Android interaction alternative only in Android documentation. For version or time wording, apply the version rules; retain other ordinary-language clauses under their matching decisions.
Apply local first-use and abbreviation rules instead of importing each Google expansion. Preserve official casing and the governing designation.
Preserve established technical meanings and domain-specific plurals. Define an unfamiliar term. Use an ordinary alternative only when no governing designation applies.
Preserve exact API, command, identifier, path, source, and product forms. Use Kubernetes in ordinary prose unless an exact source requires k8s.
Use an action or UI element name only when it matches the host. Preserve its exact label and accessible name. These entries describe the interface; they do not choose its copy.
Treat an established technical compound as terminology under its field authority, rather than changing its hyphenation mechanically.

For controls and pointer wording, apply interface naming and ambiguity rules. For image content, apply visual and media prose. W3C governs implementation, accessible names, focus, pointer events, and DOM roles.

Use the member rules for methods and fields. For parameters and their values, use the parameter rules. Distinguish query parameters, paths, ports, state transitions, and ordinary English within the documented API.
The version and time rules own the required reference point and the distinction among release order, document position, and time.
Apply the Google accessibility scope to UI documentation. Preserve exact labels and keep ARIA and DOM mechanics under W3C authority.
Review technical and figurative expressions for inclusive wording. Distinguish ordinary prose, governed terms, product names, interface labels, and unavoidable literals.
Use the governing measurement, technology, product, or host authority. Distinguish bits from bytes. Use Google's form only in its scope or exact source text.
Apply the entry's closed, hyphenated, or lowercase form in ordinary prose. A governed technical designation takes precedence over a mechanical ASD rewrite.

Use the abbreviation rules for full forms and the PM abbreviation. For an ordinary prefix or compound, apply the grammatical distinction and prefix exception. Preserve differing exact API identifiers and technical or source designations.
In technical if...then statements, retain helper words such as then when they remove ambiguity.
Use impact as a noun and a precise causal verb for the action. Apply the house leverage rule, retaining a formally governed meaning within its source scope.
Apply the existing English replacements. Retain a longer or specialised form only when it carries the required meaning.

Replace a vague or figurative technical use with the actual quality, lifecycle state, or channel. For a pejorative or socially charged expression, apply inclusive-language review. Preserve exact governed terms and defined specialised meanings.
Apply the word-choice rules to comparisons, examples, and temporal distinctions. For conjunctions, apply the punctuation and clause rules while preserving the entry's semantic distinction.
The requirement-language section owns modal meanings. Use might when the claim expresses uncertainty.
Replace the vague adjective with a measured or observable performance property. Preserve an official name only as source text.
Name or define the roles included by practitioner so readers can identify the intended audience.
Preserve a defined cryptographic, configuration, migration, or networking meaning. Otherwise name the key, use rehost, or describe the location.
The software-action rules own the login noun/verb distinction. The host's governed wording and exact label take precedence.
Name the precise mobile device, data, or network concept instead of using mobile as an unexplained noun. Preserve an official platform designation.
Prefer a direct term such as prebuilt or retrospective. Preserve COTS or blameless postmortem only as a defined governed term.
Distinguish a whole web page, a subpage of a console, a document, and documentation. Preserve the host's information model.
Use the rate rules for per and compact slash notation. When attributing a statement, apply the English according to distinction instead of using per vaguely.

Name the actual roles or relationship in generic prose. Do not pair master with slave in original prose. Identify unavoidable legacy literals. For Google product forms, apply the product-naming rules and preserve exact governed designations.
Use the version rules for release order and time. Use interface naming for UI direction. Keep Android exceptions within Android scope and distinguish document position from version order.

Apply literal formatting to ID and exact tokens. For prose, apply the English distinctions. Retain the entry-specific meanings of ingestion, N/A, internal IP address, nonce, no-op, PD, plain text, and plugin.
Use media type generally and MIME only when the standard or audience requires it. When naming the HTTP header, preserve Content-Type under literal formatting.
Use the parameter rules to distinguish an API query parameter from other parameters. For a file or resource location, use the path rules. Use simple object outside a Java audience or POJO meaning.
Apply the Google focus, dialog, form, port, key, and control distinctions. Preserve the accessible name and host action. WAI-ARIA governs implementation.
Separate each general clause from its product clauses. Preserve official terms within product scope; another host's official term or exact label controls elsewhere.
Treat rehost as a general cloud-migration strategy under the applicable migration or project taxonomy. Linked Google Cloud material supplies contextual evidence.
Replace an unmeasured quick or simple task claim with the actual requirement or duration. Retain measured speed, defined complexity, and official names.
Use time frame and white paper under the selected British convention. Reserve utilise for its established specialised sense. Preserve governed names.
Prefer Google's clearer general alternative when it preserves meaning. Retain a term defined by its legal, technical, product, security, business, or project authority.
Apply local abbreviation rules. For an English article before SQL, apply the grammatical rules to the actual pronunciation.
Apply the task-focused interaction rules, retaining required gestures, labels, protocol terms, and governed hierarchy relations. For a Google UI element name, apply its terminology adapter.
Distinguish restoring state, decompression, and archive extraction. Preserve exact commands, APIs, identifiers, menu actions, and official version labels.

Apply requirement language to obligations, permission, and capability. For genuine future, conditional, or past-habit meaning, apply English grammatical forms. Preserve governed legal, standards, contractual, and quoted wording.
Use the named person's stated pronouns or self-identification; a supposition about gender does not establish either.
Replace a vague or figurative use when a direct relation is clearer. Retain a formally established technical, professional, legal, statistical, or grammatical use.
Use typically only for what is usual or expected under normal circumstances, and keep it out of sentence-initial position. State the evidence and applicable conditions.
Replace a vague variability disclaimer with how or why results might vary.
In developer documentation, address the reader as you and use user only for someone who uses the software that the reader is developing. Preserve other defined roles.

Use the authority that governs the protocol, standard, product, legal, security, language, platform, or documentation concept. Preserve exact literals. Google's clause controls only reader-facing form.
Review technical and figurative expressions for inclusive wording. Preserve an unavoidable exact literal only where readers must identify it.
Let factual relevance, community terminology, and self-identification determine disability wording. Assess each context instead of using an unconditional replacement table.
Apply interaction rules to the reader's task and any necessary gesture. For a control name, apply the exact-label and accessible-name rules.

For quick or simple claims, apply the technical-claim rules. For a reference to a person or author, distinguish the reader, a user of the software that the reader is developing, other named roles, and the author organisation.
Pair above or below with the named cross-reference target. The house rule replaces Google's clause on document position.
Replace comprise when it obscures whether the subject is the whole or a part. The house rule replaces Google's unconditional clause.
